canonicalReview.reconciliationSummary: Both reviewers agree on nearly the whole epic: gates green (independently re-run by this canonical pass: pnpm verify-all exit 0, 366/366 tests, 44 files, process suite ran), composition discipline structural, read-only enforced at two layers, approved rulings (011 Story 3 loadCost/sourceState, 011 Story 4 threadId-normalized file equality, 023 strict-read-purity) implemented exactly, no fake or placeholder production paths. The one material disagreement is the health queue section. epic-reviewer-1 treated the listQueuedWork→report-entry-join substitution as a surface-respecting design drift ('arguably stronger for AC-4.5', observation only); epic-reviewer-2 blocked on it with a reproduced divergence (queued:5 vs 4 live work items). Independent verification confirms reviewer-2 on every link: health.ts:92-95 increments queue once per FormReportEntry with a queue join and never calls listQueuedWork; turns/internal/forms.ts:266,296 ('Both turn forms map to the one turn_derivation kind') makes one live turn_derivation work item join onto two form rows (turn_rendering + lower_band_projection); and the shipped test inspect-health.test.ts:174 itself pins queued:5 for the post-edit cascade whose owners' queue detail holds exactly 4 work items (prompt_smoothing, turn_derivation, chunk_summary_brief, chunk_summary_detailed) — so the divergence is pinned by the default suite, not edge-case-only. Epic AC-4.5's governing text ('queued and claimed work counts from the owners' queue detail') and the epic NFR ('where a report describes another surface's output ... equality is contractual') are not satisfied as written, no ruling covers the substitution (impl-log rulings 011/011/023 cover other contracts), and the tech design is internally ambiguous (Flow 4 names listQueuedWork as an input yet says 'queue = counts from the live-item joins'). Per the conservative rule, the blocker is retained, not downgraded: EV-04-001 stands as the single blocking finding (absorbing the health half of E04-ER1-002), with human-ruling scope because both fix paths alter a spec'd contract — either count work items from queue detail (breaking the queued+claimed = pending+retrying identity TC-4.1 leans on) or ratify form-entry semantics and amend AC-4.5/tech-design wording. Reviewer-1's doc-lag finding (E04-ER1-001) and reviewer-2's (EV-04-002) are the same issue and are merged into one minor finding, fully verified against epic.md:149/156, test-plan.md:38, coverage.md:48, tech-design.md:94 (DD-4 stored-sum wording vs view-report.ts:67 measured tokens), and stories/03-view-contents-report.md ('Spec Deviations: None' despite approved ruling-011). Reviewer-1's remaining observations (overview boundary via pull.meta because ViewStatus at shared/view.ts:128-135 exposes no boundaryPosition; stale stub-era comment at cli/index.ts:473-475) were independently confirmed and retained as non-blocking. No reviewer finding was discarded as unsupported.
crossStoryFindings: Story handoffs completed as tracked: the Story 2 interim view-summary source (pull().meta) was swapped to threadView.describe in Story 3 (overview.ts:121-131), and the Story 2 inspect.view stub was replaced by the real composeViewReport — receipt-tracked risks are closed in code, not just in the log.

Shared vocabulary discipline holds: report shapes live in src/shared/inspect.ts and Story 3 consumes them without redefinition; messages.show reuses the owner's report(messageId) read (DD-2); one lifecycle script (test/fixtures/lifecycle.ts) drives all four TC-5 legs including the process-suite leg (DD-8).

Confirmed cross-story semantic drift (the blocker): Flow 4's health.queue counts form-report entries with live queue joins, while Epic 02's queue-detail surfaces (listQueuedWork) count work items — a turn_derivation work item owning both turn forms is counted twice by health (EV-04-001).

Cumulative test baseline never regressed across the four accepted stories (290 → 300 → 313 → 320 → 328 default tests); epic gate re-run for this canonical review: 366/366 tests across 44 files with the process suite executed.

All four story receipts in team-impl-log.md show accepted status with verifier PASS and disposition of every finding; approved rulings are reflected accurately in shipped code — but the health-queue substitution was never the subject of any ruling.
architectureFindings: Composition discipline is structural: domains/inspect imports only other domains' index surfaces, check-boundaries.mjs carries the inspect allowlist plus the Epic 04 source check rejecting raw storage access from domains/inspect/**, and the gate runs it; the domain-graph addition is acyclic as designed.

Read-only is enforced at two layers per DD-6: every new operation runs under touch suppression, and tests assert absence-of-delta over observable state including the Story 3 storedView field added to the snapshot.

Tech design Flow 4 is internally ambiguous and the ambiguity was resolved silently in code: the flow names listQueuedWork (both owners) as a health input and the External Contracts table lists it as 'Used by ... health', yet the same paragraph says 'queue = queued/claimed counts from the live-item joins'. health.ts implemented the latter reading and never calls listQueuedWork; no design deviation was recorded and no ruling was sought (feeds EV-04-001).

DD-5 ('overview takes boundary via status') is impossible as written: ViewStatus (src/shared/view.ts:128-135) exposes no boundaryPosition, so overview.ts:121-128 reads it from pull.meta — the only surface exposing it — at the cost of a full pull render per overview call. Surface-respecting, but unrecorded in the tech design (E04-ER1-002).

Approved public-contract deviations are implemented exactly as ruled: loadCost.bandTokens measured from pull-served band messages (view-report.ts:67, ruling-011 Story 3), sourceState/meta nullable for never-compacted threads, threadId-normalized materialized-file equality with literal pull-output hash equality (lifecycle.test.ts:17-22, ruling-011 Story 4).
Error model and CLI conventions inherited cleanly: one additive caller_error code (invalid_bounds, approved); CLI commands are thin argv-to-SDK wrappers so parity including refusals is structural.
epicCoverageAssessment: 22 of 23 ACs and 16 of 17 TCs are implemented, traceable, and green: test describe blocks name their TC/AC pairs across inspect-overview, inspect-view, messages-read, inspect-health, lifecycle, and cli-process-inspect test files; epic gate re-run by this canonical review passed (pnpm verify-all, exit 0, 366/366 tests, 44 files, process suite ran).

AC-4.5 is not conclusively covered as written: TC-4.1's and TC-4.3's shipped assertions (inspect-health.test.ts:63, :174) pin the form-entry semantics — queue equals pending+retrying entry counts — not 'work counts from the owners' queue detail'; on the post-edit cascade the pinned value (queued:5) diverges from the queue-detail work-item count (4).

AC-5.3/AC-5.4 ship as threadId-normalized file equality per approved Story 4 ruling-011 (the thread id is the design's one random value; everything else byte-identical, Date frozen so pull-output hash equality stays literal); the relaxation is principled and recorded in the story spec, but epic-level docs still carry the superseded literal wording (EV-04-002).
Zero-provider NFR verified structurally for the whole epic: inspect/list/show/describe run green under a throwing provider; the lifecycle's only provider is the registry's deterministic one.

Closeout items still owed: the M3/M4 quality-half transfer to the inference epic must be recorded, and the sanctioned PRD/tech-arch search-deferral backfill exists only as uncommitted working-tree changes (see unresolvedItems).
productionPathFindings: No fake adapters, shims, or placeholder execution paths remain on any production path: the not_implemented code survives only as vocabulary in shared/errors.ts, the Story 2 inspect.view stub was replaced by the real implementation in Story 3, and the lifecycle exercise runs the real production SDK through the production registry.

Provider posture is honest by construction: the registry contains exactly one provider (deterministic — the spec'd v1 state), there is no default provider, and the CLI fails with provider_not_configured rather than silently substituting.

Confirmed material production-path issue (EV-04-001): inspect.health's queue section reports per-form-entry counts, not live work-item counts; on the standard mutation-in-flight cascade it reports queued:5 while the owners' listQueuedWork surfaces hold 4 work items, so the report disagrees with the queue-detail surface an operator would drill into.
Cosmetic only: src/cli/index.ts:473-475 still carries the stub-era comment describing 'inspect view' as not-implemented; the route is real and in the help text (E04-ER1-003).

blockingFindings.title: Health queue counts are form-entry counts, not the queue-detail work counts AC-4.5 specifies — confirmed divergence, pinned by the shipped tests
blockingFindings.evidence: Epic AC-4.5 requires 'queued and claimed work counts from the owners' queue detail'; tech-design Flow 4 and its External Contracts table name listQueuedWork (both owners) as a health input. composeHealth (src/domains/inspect/internal/health.ts:40-106) reads only messages.report + turns.report and increments queue once per FormReportEntry carrying a queue join (lines 89-95); it never calls listQueuedWork. The divergence is structural: the turns report join maps BOTH turn forms (turn_rendering, lower_band_projection) to the one turn_derivation work-item kind (src/domains/turns/internal/forms.ts:266,294-301), so one live turn-derivation item is counted twice. The shipped default suite pins the divergent value: inspect-health.test.ts:174 asserts queue {queued:5, claimed:0} for the post-edit cascade whose owners' queue detail holds exactly 4 work items (prompt_smoothing, turn_derivation, chunk_summary_brief, chunk_summary_detailed) — matching epic-reviewer-2's independent reproduction. This violates AC-4.5's source clause and the epic NFR 'where a report describes another surface's output ... equality is contractual', and no approved ruling covers the substitution. Human ruling required because both fix paths alter spec'd contract text: counting work items from queue detail breaks the queued+claimed = pending+retrying identity the current TC-4.1 assertion leans on, while ratifying form-entry semantics requires amending AC-4.5, tech-design Flow 4/External Contracts, and the test-plan TC-4.1 spine.

blockingFindings.title: Health queue counts do not match queue-detail work counts
blockingFindings.evidence: Epic AC-4.5 requires queued and claimed work counts from owner queue detail; tech-design Flow 4 says `health` composes `messages.report` + `turns.report` + `listQueuedWork` both owners. In `src/domains/inspect/internal/health.ts:40-105`, `composeHealth` only reads `messages.report` and `turns.report`, then increments `queue` once for every report entry with `entry.queue` at lines 89-95. In an ad hoc mutation-in-flight fixture, `inspect.health` returned `healthQueue:{queued:5,claimed:0}` while `messages.listQueuedWork` + `turns.listQueuedWork` returned four work item ids: `w-m5-prompt_smoothing-v2`, `w-t2-turn_derivation-v2`, `w-c1-chunk_summary_brief-v2`, `w-c1-chunk_summary_detailed-v2`.

nonBlockingFindings.title: Accepted deviation wording is not propagated through all epic-level artifacts
nonBlockingFindings.evidence: Story 4 and ruling-011 accept materialized-file equality after substituting only the random threadId, and tests implement that in `test/lifecycle.test.ts:97-103` and `:282-302`. The epic and test plan still say materialized files are byte-identical without that qualifier at `epic.md:149-157` and `test-plan.md:38-39`. Story 3/ruling-011 accepts measured pull-served `loadCost.bandTokens` and nullable `sourceState`, while `tech-design.md:94` still says `loadCost.bandTokens` is the sum of stored band counts and `stories/03-view-contents-report.md:119-121` still says no deviations.
